provenance: Original app prompts retained with stable legacy IDs. Game instructions and text-only conversation/challenges are original editorial material for two people, not copied from the protected workbook. Curate together with the separately supplied jokes/trivia supplement.

Would you rather have flat calm for a week or a 3-knot tailwind for a day?
Would you rather have unlimited chocolate or unlimited coffee on board?
Would you rather see a whale or see another boat?
Would you rather always row at dawn or always row at dusk?
Would you rather have one big storm now or constant light headwinds?
Why don’t oceans ever get bored?

items.answer: You’d think R… but it’s the C.

items.prompt: The Atlantic is the world’s ___-largest ocean.
Roughly how wide (nautical miles) is a mid-Atlantic row, La Gomera to Antigua?
items.answer: About 2,600–3,000 nautical miles; route-dependent. Entertainment estimate, not navigation guidance.
items.source: Original gROW Ocean app; approximate route estimate

items.prompt: What does VMG stand for?
Polaris sits above which celestial point?
What colour is a boat’s port navigation light?
items.answer: Red. Entertainment only; use approved navigation training at sea.

items.prompt: 20 Questions
items.instructions: One person silently chooses an everyday object, animal or place and states the category. The other asks up to 20 yes/no questions; a guess counts as a question. The chooser answers yes, no or unknown (unknown does not count). A correct guess wins; otherwise reveal after question 20. Swap roles. Agree that either person can pause without using a question.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-player instructions for a traditional game

items.prompt: Would You Rather?
items.instructions: Choose the Would You Rather category and draw a prompt. Both choose one option, then explain why. Take turns adding one harmless condition and decide whether it changes your choices. No points and no right answer. Finish after three prompts or whenever either person wants to pause.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-player instructions

items.prompt: Two Truths and a Lie
items.instructions: One person says three short things about themselves: two true and one invented. The other may ask one question about each statement, then identifies the lie. Reveal and share the story behind one truth. Swap roles for one round each. Pass on anything personal; keep topics comfortable for both.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-player instructions for a traditional game

items.prompt: Word Chain
items.instructions: Agree a category, such as foods. One person names an item. The next names an item starting with the final letter of that word. Do not repeat an item within the round. If a player cannot think of one, both may pass and start a new chain. Aim for ten words together; no timer is needed.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-player instructions for a traditional game

items.prompt: Categories
items.instructions: Agree one category and a starting letter, such as animals beginning with S. Alternate naming an example that fits. Repeated answers do not count. If both run out, count the distinct answers together, then choose a new category and letter. Play cooperatively or award one point per distinct answer.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-player instructions for a traditional game

items.prompt: Name 10
items.instructions: Choose an everyday category, such as breakfast foods or things in a library. Work together, taking turns, to name ten different examples. Count aloud or on the phone. If stuck, the other person can help or you can change category. Complete ten to finish the round; this version has no time pressure.
items.source: Original app Name 10 title; text-only, untimed two-person adaptation

items.prompt: Five-question micro-quiz
items.instructions: Select Trivia and draw five questions one at a time. Both offer an answer before revealing. Award yourselves one shared point when either answer matches; discuss near misses generously. Next advances to an unseen question. End after five or pause anytime; the app keeps category progress but you keep the round score yourselves.
items.source: Original app Trivia of the Day title; original two-person instructions

items.prompt: Story Build
items.instructions: Agree a setting and a main character. Take turns adding one sentence to the story, accepting what the previous sentence established. After eight sentences, each adds one closing sentence. End there or give the story a title together. Speak only; no recording or device handling is required.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-player instructions

items.prompt: Memory Ladder
items.instructions: Start with “I packed a…” and name one object. The other repeats that object and adds another. Continue repeating the list in order before adding one new object. If someone forgets, give a friendly clue and try again together. Finish at ten objects, or agree a shorter list. No penalties for pausing.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-player instructions for a traditional game

items.prompt: Spot the Positive
items.instructions: Each person names one small good thing from the day, without repeating the other’s example. Alternate until you have three each. The listener may ask one gentle follow-up question. There is no score; passing is allowed. Finish by choosing a shared highlight.
items.source: Original app game title; original two-person conversation instructions

items.prompt: Imagined scavenger hunt
items.instructions: Choose an imaginary setting, such as a market or a museum. Take turns naming things you could find there, working through A to Z together. Skip a letter if neither has an idea. Finish when you reach Z. This replaces the prototype photo hunt: it requires no photography, searching the boat or moving around.
items.source: Original app scavenger-hunt title; original text-only adaptation

items.prompt: Beat Your Best — word edition
items.instructions: Choose a long word, such as ENTERTAINMENT. Together make shorter words using only its letters, never using a letter more often than it occurs in the original. No proper names; agree on unfamiliar words. Count distinct answers when both want to stop. On a later round choose a new word and try to beat that count. No knots, stretches or physical tasks.
items.source: Original app micro-challenge title; original text-only replacement

items.prompt: Joke or Riddle Round
items.instructions: Choose Jokes & riddles. Read one prompt without revealing its answer. Each person may suggest a punchline or solution, then tap Reveal answer. Enjoy alternative answers rather than scoring correctness. Take turns reading; finish after three items or pause whenever needed.
items.source: Original app Joke / Riddle of the Day title; original two-person instructions

items.prompt: Which ordinary moment from home would you like to bottle and bring aboard? Take turns describing the sounds and smells.
Plan a tiny, imaginary café together. What three things are on its menu, and what is it called?
What skill would you enjoy learning simply for fun after the crossing? No productivity goals allowed.
Tell the story of a small kindness you still remember. Passing is always fine.
Imagine a museum of this crossing. Which three objects would you display, and what would their labels say?
Choose a place you would each love to revisit. What would the first hour there look like?
Invent a completely unnecessary award for each other, celebrating a harmless little habit.
Build an imaginary festival together: its name, headline activity and signature snack.
Which fictional home would be the nicest place to spend a rainy weekend? Explain your choice.
Describe your ideal entirely unscheduled day. Compare which parts you would share and which you would spend separately.
What is something you changed your mind about after trying it? Keep it light: food, music, hobbies or places.
Choose five words for a postcard to your future selves. You must agree on the final five together.
Invent three new names for a spoon without using the words spoon, food or eating. Take turns; no timer.
Tell a five-sentence story together in which each sentence starts with the next vowel: A, E, I, O, U.
Describe an imaginary sandwich using only words starting with S. Each person adds an ingredient.
Think of five different uses for an imaginary empty cardboard box. Alternate ideas and allow wonderfully impractical ones.
Summarise a familiar film in exactly six words. Let the other person guess it, then swap.
Make an alliterative name for an imaginary shop, then invent its very peculiar best-selling item.
Build a list of ten things smaller than a mug. Take turns and avoid naming the same thing twice.
Create a friendly alien greeting together. Decide what each invented word means and try a two-line conversation.
Describe a favourite meal as if explaining it to someone who has never encountered human food.
Name an imaginary island, then agree on its flag, most popular hobby and one amusing local custom.
